title: Run the Three-Way Match on the Batch
subtitle: Compute variance and tolerance for every matchable invoice
scenario: It is 11:15 AM. The duplicate is pulled and the unknown-vendor invoice is blocked, so three invoices reach the match: INV-59001, INV-59002, and INV-59005. For each, compute the price variance, compare it to the band, and check the receipt - then let the numbers declare which pass and which fail.
input: Tolerance band per invoice = larger of 2% of the PO or 25.00; quantity must match exactly. INV-59001: invoice 1200.00 vs PO 1200.00, received 500 of 500. INV-59002: invoice 1230.00 vs PO 1140.00, received 300 of 300. INV-59005: invoice 1000.00 vs PO 992.00, NO receipt posted.
instructions: For each invoice compute variance = invoice total - PO total.
Compute variancePct = variance / PO total * 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
Set toleranceBand = the larger of 2% of the PO and 25.00 (all three land at 25).
Set withinTolerance (variance within the band) and qtyMatch (received equals ordered - false when no receipt).
Return a JSON array of the three rows with numbers as numbers, then validate.
copilotPrompt: For three invoices compute variance (invoice - PO), variancePct (variance / PO * 100 to 2 decimals), toleranceBand (larger of 2% of PO or 25), withinTolerance, and qtyMatch. INV-59005 has no receipt so qtyMatch is false. Return a JSON array with numbers.
successMessage: Batch matched. INV-59001 is clean, INV-59002 fails on price, INV-59005 fails on the missing receipt.
editorHelper: One row per matchable invoice - the numbers decide.

intro.heading: Before the fork: reconcile every matchable invoice

sections.title: Only three invoices reach the match
sections.body: The duplicate (INV-58962) is already held and the unknown-vendor invoice (INV-59004) is blocked before matching. That leaves INV-59001, INV-59002, and INV-59005 to reconcile against their POs and receipts.

sections.title: The math is the same, the outcomes differ
sections.body: Variance is invoice minus PO; the band is the larger of 2% or $25. INV-59001's gap is $0, INV-59002's is $90 (outside), and INV-59005's is $8 (inside). Same rule, three different results.

sections.title: A missing receipt breaks the quantity leg
sections.body: INV-59005's price is fine, but with no posted receipt you cannot confirm the goods arrived, so qtyMatch is false. Price within tolerance plus an unconfirmed delivery is still not a clean match.

takeaway.heading: Batch matched
points: You reconciled the three matchable invoices, computing variance and percent from the totals rather than judging by eye.
INV-59001 is a clean match: $0 variance, within tolerance, quantity confirmed.
INV-59002 fails on price - a $90 variance is well outside its $25 band.
INV-59005 fails on the missing receipt - price is fine but the quantity leg cannot be confirmed.
The workflow can now decide, on numbers alone, which invoices in the batch are clean and which are exceptions.
